newsitem.title: USA: NHL-NEW YORK FANS HOWL AS RANGERS BEAT COYOTES.
newsitem.headline: NHL-NEW YORK FANS HOWL AS RANGERS BEAT COYOTES.

text.p: Wayne Gretzky and company had Ranger fans howling in appreciation on Monday as New York extended its unbeaten streak to seven games with a 5-2 defeat of the Phoenix Coyotes.
The howling may have been intended to mock the Coyotes, but the appreciation was genuine as Niklas Sundtrom scored a pair of first-period goals and Gretzky assisted on three Rangers tallies.
The three-point night by the Great One vaulted Gretzky into the National Hockey League scoring lead with 40 points.
Second-period goals by Bill Berg, Alexei Kovalev and rookie Daniel Goneau helped the suddenly hot Rangers reach the .500 mark with a 13-13-5 record.
The Rangers took advantage of a Phoenix goaltending change between the first and second periods to break open a 2-1 game.

Darcy Wakaluk gave up two goals on just seven shots in the first period, prompting the change in the Coyotes net. But Nikolai Khabibulin fared no better, surrendering goals on the first two shots he faced.
Goneau's powerplay goal made it 5-2 just over six minutes into the middle period.
Dallas Drake and Oleg Tverdovsky scored for the Coyotes, who had won four of their previous five games.
Rangers goaltender Mike Richter stopped 31 shots and was especially sharp in the first period when he turned back 14 of 15 Phoenix shots on goal.
"We got a lot of shots but Richter stood tall in there," said Phoenix coach Don Hay.
In Boston, Steve Rucchin, Teemu Selanne and Brian Bellows each had a goal and an assist to lead the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim to a 5-2 victory over the Bruins.
Joe Sacco and Ted Drury also scored for the Ducks, who are 4-1-1 in their last six games.
Rob Dimaio and Kyle McLaren scored 44 seconds apart for Boston as the Bruins tied the game at 2-2 before the second period was three minutes old.
But Drury put Anaheim back in front at 9:06 of the second with the first of three unanswered Anaheim goals.

Guy Hebert started in goal for the Ducks but was forced to leave with 4:51 left in the second period after taking a stick to the head. He was replaced by Mikhail Shtalenkov, who stopped all 11 shots he faced, including just three shots on goal by the Bruins in the third period.
In Chicago, Kirk Muller scored a pair of powerplay goals and Felix Potvin made 29 savesots as the Toronto Maple Leafs snapped a nine-game road losing streak with a 3-1 victory over the Blackhawks.
Wendel Clark assisted on both of Muller's goals and Todd Warriner iced the victory with an empty-net goal.
Mats Sundin set up Clark's second tally, moving him into a tie for second place in the NHL scoring race with 39 points.
Alexei Zhamnov was the only Blackhawk to beat Potvin when he scored a powerplay marker at 16:36 of the second period to cut the deficit to one goal.
But Potvin turned back all 11 shots he faced in the third period.
